Positions of rows and columns, for connecting plots

Source: R/anchors.R
calor_anchors.Rd

Gives the position of named rows or columns in the cell coordinates of calor_gtable(), after clustering, ordering and splitting, on one edge of the cells. Use it as the anchors of a ggcalor plot in ggweave, to draw threads from a row or column to the same item in another plot.

Usage

calor_anchors(
  plot,
  rows = NULL,
  cols = NULL,
  side = NULL,
  outside = TRUE,
  id = "id"
)

Arguments

plot

A ggcalor() plot.

rows, cols

Names of rows or columns. Give one of them.

side

Edge of the cells the anchors sit on: "left" or "right" for rows (default "right"), "top" or "bottom" for columns (default "bottom"), or "centre" for the middle of the row or column.

outside

If TRUE (default), anchors on an edge sit beyond the trees and tracks on that side, so threads do not cross them.

id

Name of the identifier column.

Value

A data frame with columns id, x and y.

Examples

m <- matrix(rnorm(20), 4, 5, dimnames = list(letters[1:4], LETTERS[1:5]))
p <- ggcalor(m) + calor_dendro(rows = TRUE)
calor_anchors(p, rows = c("a", "c"))
#>   id   x y
#> 1  a 5.5 2
#> 2  c 5.5 1
